description: Deterministic Miller-Rabin primality test for big integers.

faqs.a: A deterministic Miller-Rabin test with the known-good bases 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, which is exact for every integer below 2^64 — no probability involved.
Big integers are handled natively with BigInt, exact up to 2^64. Larger inputs are rejected rather than tested imprecisely.
faqs.q: How big can the number be?

faqs.a: By trial division with a prime sieve up to 1,000,000. If no factor is found in that range, the tool says so honestly instead of guessing.
faqs.q: How is the smallest factor found?

howto: For composites, see the smallest factor if one exists below 1,000,000.
title: Prime Number Checker
